minutes.headline: Committee ratified four union contracts and a non-affiliated plan, and kept school choice open with a gap remaining.
minutes.summary: The committee thanked outgoing members and heard line-item transfers, a superintendent report, and a building committee update. It ratified memoranda with the teachers, paraprofessionals, custodians and cafeteria workers, approved the non-affiliated benefit plan, and voted to participate in school choice with limited seats. The FY15 budget presentation left a gap, and a member asked to revisit it at the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The committee voted unanimously by roll call to ratify the teachers association memorandum of agreement, a three-year contract with cost of living increases.
Roll-call ratifications of the paraprofessionals and custodial agreements also passed unanimously; the cafeteria workers vote was not audible in the captions.
The committee approved the non-affiliated employees benefit plan.
The committee voted to take part in school choice and open seats as outlined, with none opposed.
The FY15 budget presentation left a gap after reductions, and the committee agreed to revisit it at the next meeting, possibly through more choice seats.

why_it_matters: Union contracts and the benefit plan set staffing costs for the school budget, which is largely paid from taxes, and school choice seats bring in tuition revenue that can reduce the gap the town must otherwise cover.
An unclosed FY15 school budget gap means further cuts, more choice seats or other revenue may be decided before residents are asked to vote on the budget.
